instruction_text: Speak directly to one listener with warmth and a smile in your voice; calm, steady and reassuring, like a favorite morning radio host, while keeping the news clear and credible.
asr_text: You get on the train and find a seat. At last, you can relax. Or so you think. Then you hear sounds from a video somewhere—laughter, sound effects, and cheerful music in the background. You are quietly going home, but your ears have to log into someone else's video suggestions. You paid for a train ticket, but you don't remember paying to see this show. One smartphone makes the whole train carriage an audience. That's a pretty bold show. Here's news about this kind of sound no one asks for. On October 19th, 2026, the UK announced the start of a national campaign. It asks train passengers to use headphones. But don't quickly think, in the UK, no headphones means you're breaking the law. No new rule bans all sound. The campaign points to current rail rules and asks people to think about others.
